learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous lifelong study for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and industrial engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Ability to design and calculate all structural elements and the structure as a whole with metallic elements.
Knowledge to choose the most suitable typology for particular conditions.
Ability to interpret and generate construction plans.
Knowledge of the applicable regulations for steel structures.
Ability to project, direct works and build.
Ability to control projects and execution.

syllabus_topics: BASIS OF CALCULATION. LIMIT STATES METHOD
assessment_rules: All evaluable activities are scored out of 10. To pass the course, a minimum score of 5.0 is required. In the Ordinary Call, the final course grade is the maximum of the weighted average of the progressive evaluation activities and the score of the global exam. A minimum of 4 in the theory part is required for both evaluation paths; otherwise, the final grade will not exceed 4.5. For the Extraordinary Call, the exam accounts for 100% of the grade, requiring a minimum of 5.0 overall and at least 4 in the theory part.
